note: Rewritten from Hill's English original description of 1922 (as Hamitermes germanus Hill; the original name is Termes germana Hill, 1915, Proc. Linn. Soc. N.S.W. 40: 88). The alate is described completely, with measurements; the soldier and worker are described elsewhere in the same work with Text-figs. 41, outside the window read here. Most measurements are single values.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Originally described as Termes germana (Hill 1915) and later placed in Hamitermes by Hill. Alate: head small, rounded behind the posterior margins of the compound eyes, flat in front, densely clothed with setae; postclypeus large, about 2 times as wide as long; fontanelle large, long-oval; compound eyes small (0.208×0.272), very slightly projecting; antennae 15 or 16-segmented, the segmentation variable, sometimes differing between the two sides of the same specimen.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Coloration: head deep reddish brown, thorax and abdominal tergites dark brown; labrum pale yellow; postclypeus, mouthparts, antennae, legs and underside yellow ochre; pleura brown; wings dark smoky brown, the veins dark brown. Head small, rounded behind the posterior margins of the compound eyes, flat in front, densely clothed with setae. Labrum rather small, convex at the sides, the anterior margin semicircular, clothed with setae. Anteclypeus small, transparent; postclypeus large, about 2 times as wide as long, posterior margin semicircular, the front truncate, clothed with setae. Compound eyes small (0.208×0.272), very slightly projecting, the distance to the lower margin of the head about equal to half their short diameter. Ocelli small, oval, the distance to the compound eye equal to the distance from the compound eye to the lower margin of the head. Fontanelle large, long-oval. Antennae 15 or 16-segmented, the segmentation variable, the two sides of one individual markedly different: segment 1 always short and stout, segment 2 always very short and narrow, sometimes the shortest of all, segment 3 usually shortest and narrowest but often about as long as segments 2 and 4. Pronotum small, narrower than the head, anterior margin straight, with an oblique elongate depression on each side near the midline and a smaller depression in each anterolateral region, sides rounded, concave in a wavy line towards the posterior margin, densely clothed with setae. Posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum distinctly wavy. Legs short, moderately stout, clothed with setae; tibial spur formula 3:2:2. Wing scale clothed with long and short setae, the suture straight. Wings long and narrow, the veins reaching the wing margin, the margin densely setose; membrane densely reticulate. Abdomen widest at the middle, rounded at the end, densely clothed with long and short pale setae; cerci very small. Measurements: body length (with wings) 12.5—13.0, without wings 6.5—7.0; head length 1.50, width 1.08, thickness 0.47; antennal length 1.88; pronotum length 0.61, width 0.98; forewing length 10.00, width 2.63, hindwing length 9.50, width 2.77; hind tibia length 1.17; abdominal width 1.41.
